justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the optional R4 instantiatesCanonical and instantiatesUri elements as deprecated while documenting any preferred R6 pattern.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Some legacy model clutter and possible duplicate provenance paths, but low validation ambiguity because the fields are optional and distinct.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of aligning DeviceRequest with the R6 request model is reasonable, but the supplied R6 StructureDefinition shows no native replacement for these optional protocol-definition links. Keeping them as deprecated optional elements would have preserved R4-valid instances and protocol provenance while still allowing R6 guidance to prefer another pattern. With only modest long-term cost, full removal from the base resource looks probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep `DeviceRequest.instantiatesCanonical` and `DeviceRequest.instantiatesUri` in R6 as deprecated optional elements, with text directing new implementations to the preferred R6 mechanism if one exists. That is a real base-design alternative, unlike migration-time extension preservation, because unconverted R4 instances would remain valid.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep priorRequest as a deprecated alias and/or temporarily allow broader Resource targets while adding replaces.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Aliases and broad targets preserve more R4 data but create duplicate same-resource relationship names and weaken R6 same-resource replacement validation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is coherent: use the common `replaces` request-pattern name and restrict replacement chains to DeviceRequest predecessors. A less-breaking design could have retained the old `priorRequest` name, because living with a nonoptimal R4 name is a legitimate compatibility strategy. However, preserving all R4-valid instances would also preserve broad `Reference(Resource)` targets or duplicate the relationship under two names, which carries real validation and interoperability cost.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest alternative would keep `priorRequest` as an optional deprecated alias for `replaces`, perhaps with guidance that only DeviceRequest targets are preferred in R6. This would cover common same-resource replacement cases but would either reject old cross-resource targets or keep looser target validation than the R6 design intends, so the alternative is only partial.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep required code[x] and add canonical(DeviceDefinition) as an additional choice type with clearer definitions and profile guidance.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The nonoptimal `code` name would persist and `codeCanonical` is less intuitive than `productCanonical`, but the substantive R6 product/catalog goal would be met without invalidating R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying that the ordered item is a product/device and allowing DeviceDefinition canonicals are reasonable R6 goals. The breaking rename is harder to justify because `code[x]` is mandatory in R4, so every unconverted valid R4 DeviceRequest depends on that name. Retaining the old choice name while broadening the type set would preserve essentially all R4 instances and still support the key new DeviceDefinition use case with only a moderate naming tradeoff.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would leave `DeviceRequest.code[x]` in place, update its definition to describe the requested product/device more clearly, and add `canonical(DeviceDefinition)` to the existing CodeableConcept and Reference(Device) choices. This avoids duplicate same-resource fields and makes the cost mainly cosmetic: implementers would live with the older `code` name for one more release.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep performer as Reference and retain or add a separate coded performer-role field instead of replacing the same path with CodeableReference.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves R4 reference-only performers but keeps split actor/role modeling and does not fully support CodeableReference concept-reference pairing.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Using CodeableReference is a reasonable R6 modeling goal because it lets a performer be identified by concept, reference, or both. A less-breaking design exists for common cases: keep the R4 `performer` Reference and continue using a separate coded role element. The tradeoff is material because it fails the unified representation goal and can obscure whether a code and reference are intended as one paired performer.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best compatibility design would keep `performer` as a direct Reference and carry coded performer classes in `performerType` or another optional coded field. That preserves R4 wire format for reference performers, but it is incomplete for R6 because it lacks the single CodeableReference container and requires rules to keep split fields consistent.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain performerType as a deprecated compatibility alias to performer.concept.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old coded-role data but creates duplicate role representations and requires conflict rules when both performerType and performer.concept are present.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Consolidating performer role and performer reference into a CodeableReference is coherent with the R6 performer design. Keeping `performerType` would have preserved R4 instances, but it would leave two same-resource ways to express the same performer concept and could produce conflicting or permanently duplicated representations. Those material tradeoffs make the alternative partial rather than a clean Yes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 base could keep `performerType` as optional and deprecated, define it as an alias for `performer.concept`, and warn when both are populated inconsistently. This covers R4 data well, but it undermines the consolidation goal and risks deprecated role fields accumulating indefinitely.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep reasonCode and reasonReference as deprecated aliases while adding reason CodeableReference.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves common R4 reason data but introduces competing representations and conflict or round-trip ambiguity, especially for paired concept-plus-reference reasons.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of unifying coded and linked reasons under CodeableReference is reasonable and adds expressive value, including preserving a code/reference pair as one reason. Retaining the old arrays would preserve R4 instances, but it would also create duplicate same-resource representations for reasons and weaken the single-container model. Because the less-breaking design is useful but materially incomplete and ambiguous, the break is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative would keep `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` as optional deprecated aliases for `reason[].concept` and `reason[].reference`. This avoids immediate R4 validation failures, but R6 instances with both concept and reference in one CodeableReference cannot be represented cleanly in the old split arrays without losing the pairing or adding extra metadata.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-to-R6 alternative is needed; this optional R6 modifier does not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The material risk is R6-to-R4 conversion: negation must be preserved or rejected, but extension backports are mitigations rather than base-design alternatives.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Explicit support for negative DeviceRequests is a reasonable and safety-relevant R6 goal, and making the element a modifier is appropriate because it can invert the request. This is not an old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 base-design break: R4 instances remain valid when moving forward. The compatibility concern is that R6 negative requests cannot be safely down-converted or consumed by systems that ignore the modifier.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Using an extension or profile to carry negation would be a backport or migration mitigation, not a less-breaking R6 base design for preserving R4 instances. Because the R6 field is optional and additive, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is best calibrated as Not applicable.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because optional R6 quantity and location fields preserve all R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 receivers need extension or profile policy for down-conversion; that is a mitigation for new R6 content, not a less-breaking R6 base design.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding explicit quantity and location elements is a reasonable R6 expressiveness improvement and does not make any R4-valid DeviceRequest invalid in R6. The reported compatibility issue is R6-to-R4 representability, not R4-to-R6 base breakage. Under the calibration rules, ordinary extension backports for R4 systems should not be counted as a Yes or Partial base-design alternative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The relevant compatibility path is conversion policy: preserve R6 `quantity` and `location` in extensions, a profile convention, or reject lossy down-conversion. Those choices do not indicate a less-breaking R6 base design was available because the R6 additions are forward-compatible for R4 data.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because optional R6 asNeeded and asNeededFor fields do not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extension or Timing-note conventions are down-conversion mitigations, not backward-compatible R6 base-design alternatives.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Dedicated PRN fields are a reasonable R6 goal because they reduce ambiguity in device-use instructions. Since these elements are optional additions, there is no R4-to-R6 base instance break to avoid. The compatibility risk lies in older R4 systems losing new R6 PRN semantics during down-conversion.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Relying on `occurrence[x]`, notes, or extensions for PRN semantics would avoid new R6 content but would also keep the ambiguity R6 is trying to remove. For calibration, those are R4 backport or migration strategies, not evidence of a less-breaking base R6 alternative.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; widening requester targets preserves all R4 requester references.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Older R4 validators may reject new R6 requester target types, but no less-breaking alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Supporting patient, related-person, group, and care-team requesters is a reasonable R6 workflow expansion. Because all R4 requester target profiles remain allowed, the base change is forward-compatible for R4 instances. The remaining issue is R6-to-R4 target representability and generated-code updates, so the backward-compatible alternative field should be Not applicable rather than Partial.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A profile-only widening could have limited base R6 change, but it would not be a backward-compatible alternative to an R4-to-R6 break because no such forward break exists. Down-conversion still needs policy for the added target types.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; adding ended to the R6 required status binding does not remove any R4 status code.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 enum and conversion risk requires ConceptMap or policy, but that is not an R4-to-R6 base-design alternative.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The `ended` code appears to fill a real workflow gap between completion and revocation, and no inspected R4 status code is removed. Therefore R4 instances remain valid with respect to status when moving to R6. The lack of authoritative down-conversion mapping keeps the verdict at probably justified, but the compact alternative availability should be Not applicable because the finding is a pure R6-to-R4 required-binding concern.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: An official ConceptMap or extension-preservation rule would help converters handle `ended`, but those are migration mitigations. Avoiding the new code by overloading existing R4 statuses would reduce R6 expressiveness rather than provide a needed less-breaking base design for R4-to-R6 compatibility.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; adding solicit-offer and offer-response preserves all R4 intent codes.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Older R4 enums and required bindings need mapping policy, but this is a down-conversion risk rather than a less-breaking R6 base-design choice.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The new intent codes appear to support request-offer workflows that R4 could not express directly. Because no R4 intent code is removed and the element shape is unchanged, this is not an R4-to-R6 validation break. The remaining concern is that R6 instances using the new modifier codes cannot be represented safely in base R4 without policy, so Not applicable is the calibrated alternative availability.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Using existing R4 `proposal` plus extensions or profiles would be a down-conversion/backport strategy, not a base-design alternative needed to preserve R4 instances. It would also sacrifice the R6 goal of interoperable first-class intent codes for these workflows.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Make intent immutability a best-practice warning or profile/lifecycle rule rather than base conformance text.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Softer guidance preserves more existing update workflows but weakens audit consistency for a modifier element that changes request meaning.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Preventing in-place changes to `intent` is a reasonable goal because intent modifies interpretation and affects auditability. A less-breaking approach could have introduced warning-level guidance first, but that would leave inconsistent lifecycle behavior across implementations. Since the change is semantic rather than a single-instance validation break, and the softer path only partially meets the audit-safety goal, the R6 choice is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative would express immutability as best-practice guidance, a warning invariant, or a profile rule for stricter workflows. That would reduce disruption for systems that promoted a request by updating `intent`, but it would not give base R6 consumers the same consistent guarantee about resource lifecycle semantics.
